pageCache.text:
Welcome to English Martyrs’ Catholic Primary School
Welcome to English Martyrs. We’re delighted that you’ve taken an interest in our wonderful school and hope that the pages of this website give you all the information that you need about us.
English Martyrs is a large two form entry Catholic primary situated in Reading. We’re very diverse in nature and our children come from a range of different cultures and backgrounds. However, the one thing that they have in common is that they all come to a school where Christian values are at the heart of everything we do. All in our school community our encouraged to love one another, as Christ Himself has loved us; it’s the most important thing that we teach our pupils and means that a natural compassion for everyone, flows throughout our school.
Staff go above and beyond at English Martyrs, to try to ensure that we provide each and every child, with a first-class education, regardless of their starting points. Our intention is to meet ‘every child where they are’, so that all can grow throughout their education into rounded, polite and healthy individuals and achieve their full academic and personal potential.
We are always happy to meet prospective parents and new families, so if you’d like to come in and have a look around, feel free to contact us
Key Information
We are proud that Ofsted recognised in 2024 that ‘Pupils work hard and want to be their best. They talk about the importance of respect for others and are confident that faith, hope and love are solid foundations for future happiness and success’
Our Mission is about Building a Learning Community of Faith, Hope and Love.
Nursery & EYFS
At English Martyrs’, our Nursery and Reception children engage with a creative, fun, and relevant curriculum tailored to meet their individual needs.
Curriculum
Our teaching at English Martyrs’ is carried out through a broad and rich curriculum that gives the opportunity for all to succeed and fulfil their potential.
Parents
We highly value the role that parents play in their children’s education and actively work in partnership with them, to enable our children to flourish.
Opened since July 1962
Our Newsletters
Our school Newsletters are sent direct to your e–mail, if you would like to be added please contact the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music
Our music curriculum operates by engaging pupils in four core areas: performing, composing, listening, and appraising. Children learn to sing and play instruments, create their own music, and critically listen to a diverse range of musical styles and periods. This holistic approach builds skills in rhythm, pitch, and notation while fostering creativity and self-confidence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance, Absence and Illness - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Attendance, Absence and Illness
Attendance
For a child to have high levels of educational achievement, a high level of school attendance is essential. We are committed to providing an education of the highest quality for all our pupils and endeavour to provide an environment where all pupils feel valued and welcome. Parents and pupils play a part in making our school so successful. Every child has a right to access the education to which he/she is entitled. Parents and teachers share the responsibility for supporting and promoting excellent school attendance and punctuality for all. It is our duty to consistently strive to achieve a goal of 100% attendance for all children. Every opportunity will be used to convey to pupils and their parents or carers the importance of regular and punctual attendance.
What does absence equate to in terms of pupils and their learning?
The School door opens at 8:30am.
Children must be in class and ready to start lessons by 9.00am. After this time, all children must enter via the office and be signed in by a parent or carer.
Children arriving after 9:00am will be marked as late.
All children are expected to attend school EVERYDAY throughout the academic year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clubs - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Clubs
Our after-school club program is a cornerstone of our commitment to holistic education. We believe these clubs are vital for enriching our pupils’ lives beyond the academic timetable, providing a fantastic opportunity for children to explore new passions, develop existing talents, and build confidence in a fun and supportive environment. From activities such as sports and art, to choir and board games, our diverse range of clubs allows children to learn new skills, forge friendships across different year groups, and discover hidden abilities. These experiences are invaluable in helping our pupils grow into well-rounded, resilient, and curious individuals.

pageCache.pageTitle: Tapestry Guide for Parents - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Tapestry Guide for Parents
All children who attend English Martyrs Early Years classes will have an online Learning Journey which records photos, observations and comments, in line with the Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum. This builds up a record of your child’s experiences during their time with us which you can access at any time.
We will be using Tapestry, a piece of educational software which is hosted in the UK on secure servers. These dedicated servers conform to very high security standards and are closely monitored. File names are encoded for uploaded videos and images, making Tapestry a safe, secure online Learning Journey assessment tool.
The benefits to yourselves as parents from Tapestry being online means you will have secure access to your child’s Learning Journey via a website which you log into using a unique user ID and password. Please note each parent will only have access to their own child’s Learning Journey. You will receive an email telling you when a new observation or piece of work is available for you to view. This will enable you to follow your child’s individual progress closely and you can reflect upon achievements with your child. Staff will reference your child’s learning to the Early Years profile so you will know which area of learning your child is making progress in and the relevant age band they were working in for that activity.
In addition to viewing our contributions, we encourage you to add to it by uploading your own photos and comments, so that we as a staff find out about activities your child really enjoyed and the learning that is taking place at home. You can also leave your own comments on observations we have made.
In order for your child’s Learning Journey to be created, please give us permission by completing the attached form. Please also provide your email address and we will set up an account enabling you to access your child’s Learning Journey via the secure Tapestry website. You will receive a link by email to complete the registration process on Tapestry. Please action this within one week as the link will expire for security reasons.
If you not have access to email, please still complete the permission form so that we can create an online Learning Journey and it will be possible for us to provide print outs if requested.
E-safety is extremely important to us at English Martyrs, therefore we also ask you to agree with our guidelines.
If you have any questions please do not hesitate to contact us.
Setting Up Tapestry
Throughout EYFs, Nursery and Reception, we use Tapestry as an online learning journal to show your child’s journey with us. We do this by uploading observations with photos and videos.
We encourage parents to upload your own observations as well, to show your child’s learning experiences at home. This could be photos, videos and comments of activities your child likes to do, such as baking or going on bug hunts or it could be showing work they have done like drawing a picture, writing their name, or counting objects.
We have included some videos to help you with your Tapestry account.

pageCache.pageTitle: Before School and After School Club - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Before School and After School Club
We provide quality wrap around childcare for children between 3 and 11 years old: Breakfast Club (7:30 am to 8:30 am) and Afterschool Club (3:00 pm to 6:00 pm). Staff work within the Early Years Foundation Stage framework for those children who are under six years old.
Parents can pick and choose sessions the days/sessions they need. The children take part in fun and structured activities during their time at the clubs with healthy, enjoyable meals provided as part of the cost. Children who attend the Breakfast Club are dropped off at their classroom for morning registration. They are collected from their classrooms at the end of the school day and taken to the After School Club room. We work on a ratio of one adult to six children. This is the minimum ratio required by Ofsted. Children’s individual needs will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
Breakfast and ASC encourage a play-based curriculum where children engage with their friends through social interactions This in turn develops language, self-esteem and team building skills. Worldwide and cultural themes are used effectively to enhance children’s awareness of world events. Children are discouraged from playing computer games, but children’s TV is available during long periods of wet weather and special occasions.
Bookings are on a first come first served bases. Bookings close on a Friday morning for the following week. For additional bookings there will be a £1 administration fee.
We require 48 hours’ notice of cancellation. Cancellations made out of this timeframe will not be refunded. Refunds are usually given if a child is unable to attend school due to sickness. Please inform the school office of any absences as soon as you are able. The staff:
Wraparound Care Manager: Teresa Marcham Deputy Manager: Marie Kearney
Playworkers: Kathleen Connolly, Rachel O’Gorman, Sam Parks, Deena Castelino, Devika Weerasekara and Zoe O’Gorman.
All staff are DBS checked and each session will have at least one qualified first aider.
All of our full-time staff hold first aid and food hygiene certificates. Breakfast Club – Price per session After School Club – Price per session.
Please book and pay using SchoolMoney

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Computing
Purpose of study
A high-quality computing education equips pupils to use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world. Computing has deep links with mathematics, science, and design and technology, and provides insights into both natural and artificial systems. The core of computing is computer science, in which pupils are taught the principles of information and computation, how digital systems work, and how to put this knowledge to use through programming. Building on this knowledge and understanding, pupils are equipped to use information technology to create programs, systems and a range of content. Computing also ensures that pupils become digitally literate – able to use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through, information and communication technology – at a level suitable for the future workplace and as active participants in a digital world. (National Curriculum Computing 2014)
The aims for the implementation of the Computing Curriculum are to ensure that all children:
Computing at English Martyrs
“People think computer science is the art of geniuses but the actual reality is the opposite, just many people doing things that build on each other, like a wall of mini stones.” (Donald Knunth – American computer scientist)
SUBSTANTIVE KNOWLEDGE
There are 4 key strands to the substantive computing knowledge we teach our children:
DISCIPLINARY KNOWLEDGE
There are five key areas which underpin the disciplinary knowledge and skills identified as central to pupils’ computing education and to equip them for digital life in the 21st century; part of the connected world framework. These key areas are returned to in each year group making it clear to see prior and future learning. Each time pupils revisit an area of learning they are reminded of prior knowledge which is then built upon with increasing depth and complexity.
The curriculum is led and overseen by the computing curriculum leader and SLT, who regularly monitor, evaluate and review computer teaching and learning, celebrating and sharing good practice. Formative assessments will be integrated into every day computing teaching to ensure teachers have an in–depth knowledge of the children’s learning and inform their next steps.
The National Curriculum 2014 and the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory framework 2021, together with the Development Matters non-statutory curriculum guidance 2021, provide the basis for our computer curriculum, which is then tailored to meet the learning and developmental needs of the children in our school.
Teachers’ day-to-day planning is based on the ‘Kapow Primary’ Computing Curriculum Long Term Plans. These include substantive knowledge for each area of study, and the disciplinary knowledge enabling children to think like computer scientists.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Maths
Fluency with numbers is really important for helping children learn to solve problems in all sorts of contexts.
It is important that children understand what numbers and calculations mean, rather than simply counting, etc, by rote. We support this by using lots of objects and images as children are learning new concepts. This is called a “Concrete > Pictorial > Abstract” approach to maths learning.
We use the White Rose Scheme of Work and supporting resources. Children also have access to MyMaths and Times Tables Rockstars online resources, to support practice at home.
Intent:
Mathematics is a creative and highly interconnected discipline that has been developed over centuries, providing the solution to some of history’s most intriguing problems. It is essential to everyday life, critical to science, technology and engineering, and necessary for financial literacy and most forms of employment. (National Curriculum 2013)
At English Martyrs we aim to make maths accessible to all children, to foster a love of learning mathematically and inspire future mathematicians. We want children to be confident and resilient when solving tasks and problems, as well as being able being fluent and articulate when communicating their knowledge and understanding of this critical subject.
What is Teaching for Mastery?
Mastering maths means pupils acquiring a deep, long-term, secure and adaptable understanding of the subject. The phrase ‘teaching for mastery’ describes the elements of classroom practice and school organisation that combine to give pupils the best chances of mastering maths. Achieving mastery means acquiring a solid enough understanding of the maths that’s been taught to enable pupils to move on to more advanced material. (NCETM)

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
Intent
At English Martyrs, the intention of our MFL curriculum is not only to develop an interest in other languages, but also to learn about familiar and unfamiliar cultures, taking into account the knowledge of our vast intercultural community. From Nursery to Year 6 we aim to introduce different cultural experiences during the school year, celebrating “English Martyrs language day”, “International day”, along with other events. The use of these strategies throughout the MFL curriculum will ensure the children recognise the importance of their home language and family believes (belief) and we hope to widen their love for languages and an acceptance of a multicultural world.
This year, we aim to introduce the learning of Spanish in Year 3, 4 and 5 and to continue the learning of French in year 6 in enjoyable and meaningful ways, taking into account the class background and interest. In addition to this, our mission is to embed the essential skills of listening, reading, speaking and writing, whilst we aim to broaden the children’s cultural understanding by the awareness of similarities and differences between familiar and unfamiliar cultures.
MFL is taught in an inclusive way, tailoring the content to reach the children’s needs and interests. The lessons are taught using a wide range of strategies such as songs, rhymes, debates, flashcards, and delivering the content using the different learning styles. These strategies support us to engage all pupils and to reach each child’s necessity/needs.
Our language lessons are planned to meet the needs of all children including SEN children, those who show a particular strength in MFL and children for whom English is an additional language. Our principal aim will be to develop the children’s knowledge, skills and understanding with suitable tasks that challenge and promote equity among all.
How are we implementing our transition:
In response to our community interest we have decided to change our language. To ensure a smooth transition and high standards of teaching and learning in MFL, this school year we have introduced Spanish to year 3, year 4 and year 5 we are offering French to our 6 class. The MFL curriculum in our school is based upon the Primary National Curriculum in England, which provides a broad framework that outlines the knowledge and skills taught. We have introduced “Angel Languages”, an interactive and fun Spanish and French programme. Each unit lasts one half term and each of them cover a topic. The children learn different grammar structures, vocabulary, phonics and expressions, giving them the resources to use their language knowledge in daily situations. In addition, this programme has a clear progressive structure which ensures knowledge and skills are built upon.
In MFL, skills in speaking, reading, understanding and writing another language are taught through songs, interactive games, fun activities and repetition. From the beginning of the year, children are introduced to the grammar structure in Spanish and French, phonemes and development of simple sentences in both languages.
The impact we would like to make:
Here at English Martyrs we love to support our pupils and to offer them a wide range of experiences to ensure their success in their new journey. With our MFL curriculum we aim at the end of KS2, pupils will have developed a good foundation that will prepare them to:

pageCache.pageTitle: SEN & Inclusion - English Martyrs Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
SEN & Inclusion
As a Catholic school, the staff and governors of English Martyrs recognise that each child is made in the image and likeness of God. We are all equal before God, but He has made each one of us in a special and unique way. Subsequently we are all given different talents and abilities.
With this spirit in mind, the school strives to ensure that all children are treated equally and included fully in every aspect of school life. It is our aim to provide the highest quality of education for all of our pupils, whatever their background, ability or need. English Martyrs fully supports the government’s aims expressed in the Children and Families Act 2014. We therefore aspire to ensuring that every child has the chance to fulfil their potential by being challenged and stretched and encouraged to achieve their potential in every circumstance.
